title: Edit raw videos by giving notes to your agent
summary: A developer packaged a free skill that lets Claude Code cut, caption and add motion graphics to raw videos, then learns the creator's notes as lasting style rules.
agent_role: The agent installs tools, transcribes the clip, cuts dead air, adds captions, zooms, color and sound, and renders drafts. The person watches each draft and gives notes until saying final.
outcome: Author reports it was tested on Windows 11 with Claude Code for setup, test render, transcription and cutting.
what_they_did: A developer built free247editor, a set of instructions a coding agent follows to edit video. You drop a raw clip in an inbox folder and say "edit this". The agent transcribes it, removes pauses and retakes, adds captions, zooms and music, and saves a draft. You give notes in plain words, and lasting ones are saved as rules for future edits.
how_it_went: The author says it was tested on Windows 11 with Claude Code. Other agents and Mac or Linux are not tested yet.
worth_knowing: Editing uses a lot of your agent plan's usage; the author suggests a higher Claude plan if you edit often. It never posts videos for you.
prompt: Set up a video editing workflow in [folder]. Install what's missing only after asking me (FFmpeg, a free transcription option). Then take the raw video in [inbox folder]: transcribe it, cut dead air, breaths and retakes, add word-by-word captions in [caption style], a hook in the first 3 seconds, gentle zoom-ins, and background music from [my sounds folder]. Export a vertical 9:16 draft to [outbox folder] and wait for my notes. Save any lasting notes I give as rules in a file and apply them to every future edit. Don't call any paid service or upload anything without asking.

curation.rationale: A free, reproducible setup that turns a coding agent into a video editor that learns your notes, with clear steps; but no concrete results or sample edits are reported beyond testing on Windows with Claude Code.
